assumptions: one App Runner instance, 1 vCPU / 2 GB, left running continuously for a 30-day demonstration period
App Runner bills provisioned memory continuously and vCPU only while a request is being served
judge and demo traffic on the order of a few thousand requests over the period, which is a rounding error against the idle memory charge
one 11.4 MB model object in S3 and a few thousand small DynamoDB items under a 14-day TTL
public AWS list prices as published for us-east-1; no credits applied
cost_controls_in_place: DynamoDB on-demand billing rather than provisioned capacity
14-day TTL on trace records so the table cannot grow without bound
uploads not retained, so no storage accrues from inspections
one instance, one worker; no autoscaling floor above 1
ECR scan-on-push only, no continuous scanning
dominant_cost: provisioned App Runner memory while idle. Everything else - S3 for a single 11 MB object, on-demand DynamoDB for a few thousand small items, ECR for one image, CloudWatch for modest JSON logs - is negligible beside it.
how_to_stop_all_charges: delete the App Runner service; the S3 object, DynamoDB table and ECR image cost approximately nothing at this size
order_of_magnitude: single-digit to low-tens of US dollars per month
purpose: show the architecture is intentionally small, not to predict a bill
why_no_precise_figure: A precise monthly number would be invented. Actual cost depends on the current published rates, how long the service is left running, and how much traffic arrives - none of which has been observed over a full billing period. The account's existing baseline is a separate matter from this stack.
